dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quarterly guidance published (sector convention: annual guidance only). Qualitative H2 signals given on the call: European peak season running as expected ('not significantly worse or better'), progressive UK volume recovery through H2 2026 and more visibly into 2027, and a robust free-cash-flow acceleration expected in H2 after a CapEx-heavy H1 (H1 FCF ~EUR 30M).
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY2026 guidance reiterated unchanged at H1 (23/07/2026 call): EBITDA about EUR 450M, EPS growth above 5%, underlying free cash flow around EUR 200M excluding restructuring costs. CapEx to stay intentionally elevated at EUR 170-180M/year (above replacement level, no normalization before 2027 at the earliest) without distorting the FCF trajectory. CEO acknowledges in Q&A (Kepler) that the implied H2 looks mathematically conservative after the strong H1, but keeps the guidance prudent citing energy-cost volatility, still-excessive competition and ongoing UK and Chile restructuring plans.
pointsCles: Margin discipline through the volume trough: H1 26 EBITDA of EUR 225.5M, margin 29.9% (+110bp YoY) despite organic sales -3.8% cc (price effect -1.8%); Q2 volumes group -0.6% with Europe back positive at +1.5%, UK/Ireland -7% (improving vs -9% in Q1) and South America +4%; Q2 pricing: Southern Europe -4.3%, UK/Ireland -0.4%, South America +3.5% (local inflation).

Fortress balance sheet funding an extraordinary return: net debt EUR 252M (0.6x pro forma LTM EBITDA) even after the Chile acquisition (EV EUR 75M, consolidated from 01/01/2026), the February interim dividend and heavy H1 CapEx; 2026 dividend raised +15% (>EUR 62M) and the buyback extended twice from 1% to 3% of capital (max EUR 90M) - total shareholder returns above EUR 150M this year.

UK turnaround on track and intentional market-share recapture: volumes lost ~a year ago to 'abnormal levels of competition' (mostly imports) to be recovered within 18 months max - not fully in 2026 - helped by adapted costs, adjusted prices and importers now suffering renewed inflation; UK profits and margins described as broadly safe, UK/Ireland reaffirmed as core; CEO calls the group's share gains 'not a perception, a conviction', executed with financial discipline.

Energy locked and outlook conservative by design: ~70% of 2026 and ~60% of 2027 energy exposure hedged via derivatives (nearly all European/UK exposure fixed for the rest of 2026) on top of contractual pass-through formulas; management sees no negative pricing move nor price/cost spread deterioration risk in 2027 despite Middle East-driven energy tension; CEO concedes the implied H2 (guidance ~EUR 450M EBITDA vs consensus 450-451M) looks mathematically conservative but declines to raise - 'keep an eye on next year'; note the departure of Corporate Finance Director Inigo Mendieta, with IR folded into corporate development under Galo Alvarez.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Resilient glass-packaging producer with stable margins: despite organic demand still in decline (-3.8% cc), H1 26 delivered EBITDA margin +110bp to 29.9%, EBIT +30bp to 20.2%, and net +8.9% (117.4M). South America (Chile) clearly outperforms (sales +14% pro forma, EBITDA margin 37.6% - the highest of the three zones). FY26 guidance reiterated: EBITDA >450M, EPS +5%+, FCF ~200M, with an explicit H2 cash-generation acceleration.

== THESIS READ ==
- Margin discipline through a volume trough is the thesis proof - pricing/cost control beats demand softness. Watch: volume inflection in core Iberia/UK.
- Chile is becoming the growth and margin engine - the 2025 acquisition already carries the group print. Watch: Chile margin durability and any further LatAm build-out.
- Share-count correction (Nov-2025 bonus issue undercounted at creation: 34.5M vs 33.8M) trims Omnium EPS 0.6% BELOW the guided +5% floor - an honest wedge, to re-arbitrate at Q3. Watch: weighted-average count at FY26.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
'ebit' = operating result after depreciation (NOT the guided EBITDA >450M, which sits ~160M above). 2024 published net (~= EBIT) carried the Italy-disposal gain - handled in the historical series. Low debt (230 -> 80M), near-zero financial result; ETR 18% blended (21% actual 2025). Buyback-driven count decline resumes from 2027 in the model.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 1,500M, EBIT 288M (19.2%), EPS 6.86; 2027-2030: revenue +3%/yr, EBIT margin ~19.3-20%, shares -1.5%/yr from 2027. Watch: share count; energy-cost hedges; UK consumer demand; Chile FX.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 trading update (Oct); H2 FCF acceleration proof; FY26 results (Feb 2027); LatAm expansion moves.

ancrages.moteur: FY2026 guidance reiterated unchanged at H1 26 (EBITDA >450 M€, EPS +5%+, FCF ~200 M€), with an acceleration in cash generation expected in H2 explicitly mentioned by management. The CEO acknowledges in the Q&A (Kepler Cheuvreux question) that the EBITDA consensus (~450-451 M€) could look conservative given the H1 run-rate, but maintains a cautious stance ('too early', 'keep an eye on next year') without formally raising guidance - retained as such in the model, no upward adjustment injected on the basis of an unquantified statement.

South America (Chile) in confirmed strong growth: sales H1 26 +14% pro forma, EBITDA margin 37,6% (the highest of the three regions, though down vs 38,5% a year earlier), Q2 volumes +4%+ and prices +3,5% (local inflation) - the group's most solid growth and margin driver. The CEO confirms he is still in the platform build-out phase (entered ~2 years ago), with regional M&A opportunities explored but not committed at this stage.

European and UK demand still sluggish but improving sequentially: Europe volumes +1,5% in Q2 (prices -3%), UK&Ireland volumes -7% in Q2 but markedly improved vs Q1 (-9%), with the CEO anticipating a gradual recovery of the lost volumes spread over 2026-2027 (not entirely this year) thanks to less intense competition from importers, themselves under inflationary pressure.

Weighted average share count H1 26 (~34,9M, computed from the reported EPS and net income) markedly above the creation assumption (33,8M for the full year) - effect of the November 2025 bonus share issue initially underestimated.

Extraordinary extension of the share buyback programme to 3% of capital (announced with the H1 26 results, in two steps from an initial 1%), with a cancellation objective - total shareholder remuneration envelope >150 M€ in 2026, consuming a significant share of the expected FCF and gradually reducing the share count over the projection horizon (partial offsetting effect to the dilution from the bonus shares).

Net debt at 30/06/2026 of 252,3 M€ (0,6x pro forma LTM EBITDA), virtually flat since end-March (273 M€) despite positive FCF, on the back of the dividend increase (+15%) and the extension of the buyback programme - the 'virtually debt-free' narrative floated at Q1 26 is invalidated by this refresh; deleveraging trajectory revised markedly upward (less reduction) across the whole projection horizon. CapEx deliberately high (~8% of revenue, vs ~4% of normative maintenance) confirmed as intentional by the CEO, with no normalisation before 2027 at the earliest - does not compromise the FCF trajectory if operating profits continue to grow.
